brief: Ian's read on the first ToC commit: unclear where the homepage's 'Contents' links came from (they're the homepage's own two section headings — not very useful there), and asked to fold it into the existing eyebrow metadata row on note pages rather than a separate block.
fixed: Removed the ToC from index.njk entirely — the homepage's 2 short section headings didn't justify a jump-to-section aid, and it visually competed with the hero right above it. Kept on note.njk (newsletter issues / notes), where long-form content actually benefits.

Moved the <details class="dl-toc"> element to live inside .header-meta (the same row as tags/timestamps, both currently off by default) instead of as a separate bordered block below the whole header. .dl-toc-summary now inherits header-meta's mono/uppercase/tracked eyebrow voice by CSS inheritance rather than redeclaring it.

header-meta is now display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap so multiple eyebrow items (tags, timestamps, Contents) sit on one compact line when they fit. .dl-toc[open] gets flex-basis:100%, so the expanded link list claims the full row width and wraps onto its own line rather than being squeezed into a narrow flex slot — pure CSS, no JS.

validation.archiveConfirmed: 0 dl-toc matches — page.njk was never wired for ToC, unaffected

brief: Ian enabled dgShowToc and republished; the ToC went live on production but rendered at the very end of the article (sidebar.njk's <aside>, right before the footer) — defeating its purpose as a jump-to-section accessibility aid. Asked Hallmark to determine the best placement given DL's canonical contract explicitly forbids sidebars.
findingsBeforeFix: sidebar.njk bundled ToC together with backlinks/local-graph in one end-of-article <aside>, all currently unused except ToC.

The plugin's base .toc CSS (digital-garden-base.scss) has @media (max-width: 1400px) { .toc { display: none; } } — a leftover from the original floating-sidebar design that only had room on very wide screens. This silently broke visibility at every normal viewport width once the ToC was moved in-flow, and took real CDP-level CSS debugging to find (it wasn't visible via querying document.styleSheets — the media-rule nesting made it easy to miss).
fixed: Extracted the ToC-specific block out of sidebar.njk into its own components/tableOfContents.njk, included right after the article <header> (before body content) in note.njk and index.njk. sidebar.njk keeps its backlinks/local-graph/dynamics-hooks responsibility, unchanged, still positioned at the end of the article where that content type belongs.

Wrapped it in a native <details>/<summary> disclosure — collapsed by default so it doesn't push every article down, expands via native browser keyboard/ARIA semantics (Enter/Space on the focused summary), zero custom JS needed for the toggle itself. The open/closed +/− glyph swap is pure CSS ([open] attribute selector).

Kept the plugin's existing .toc/.toc-container classes and all their nesting/indent/hover/active-state CSS as-is inside the new wrapper — that logic was already solid, only the outer wrapper and position needed to change.
Overrode the legacy 1400px display:none rule scoped to .dl-toc specifically, so it doesn't affect the old rule's original intent anywhere else it might still apply.
Overrode --dg-toc-max-height (70vh, sidebar-scroll-box sizing) to none — the in-flow list should never need internal scrolling.

validation.keyboard: pass — details/summary native toggle confirmed via actual Enter-key activation, not a click simulation; collapsed by default confirmed on load
validation.scrollSpyPreserved: pass — the active-heading-highlight-on-scroll script was relocated along with the ToC markup, not lost

brief: Digitally Literate newsletter and curated public notebook
decisions: Public note types are Evergreen, Grove, and Forest.
Seed, Sprout, and Plant remain private development states.
Light mode is the default reading surface; explicit reader choice persists.
Texture is limited to semantic Apparatus regmarks, never resting-state backgrounds or body text.
Homepage rhythm uses a compact named spacing scale and avoids inherited plugin block margins.
Homepage illustration is a decorative grove, not a maturity-stage taxonomy mark.
The masthead retains the full Digitally Literate name.
The homepage title remains on one line while the earlier geometric grove form supplies the counterweight.
Evergreen motion is isolated to the tree forms; the grove baseline remains fixed.
